title: The 10 Best Wi-Fi Temperature and Humidity Sensors
subtitle: Sensors and kits that send alerts to your phone, no smart home hub needed.
intro: We pulled the Wi-Fi temperature and humidity monitors selling on Amazon and scored them on rating, review volume, and features: alerts, data history, and probes. Several popular kits use Bluetooth or their own radio to a Wi-Fi gateway; the table shows which.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

awards.label: Best Overall
awards.name: Govee H5179
awards.why: Direct Wi-Fi with no gateway, ±0.54°F accuracy, 7,910 reviews, and 2K+ bought last month.

reasons: The bullets are five short phrases, like "Quick Setup" and "Unlimited Users."
No accuracy, battery life, or power source is given in the bullets.
Humidity isn't mentioned anywhere in the title or bullets.

buyers_guide.a: Most smart sensors are within about 1°F and 3 to 5% relative humidity, which is fine for rooms, nurseries, and basements. For fridges, freezers, or reptile tanks, pick one with a probe or a stated tighter accuracy, and check it against a reference thermometer once.

buyers_guide.q: What can I automate with one?
buyers_guide.a: Turn on a fan or dehumidifier when humidity climbs, get an alert when a freezer warms up or pipes risk freezing, or let a smart thermostat average temperatures across rooms.

buyers_guide.q: How long do the batteries last?
buyers_guide.a: Most battery sensors on these lists are rated for one to three years, depending on how often they report. Low-power radios like Zigbee, Z-Wave, and Thread last much longer than Wi-Fi.
